language_task: Pick up the pen with the right hand and the cap with the left hand, then fit the cap onto the pen.
outcome_evidence: The supplied task redundantly says “pen cap” and “cap”; the visible pen and separate cap support the intended capping task stated above. Frames 271–400 in right_wrist, left_wrist and top show acquisition and bringing the parts together. The cap is not successfully seated: at frames 744–766, left_wrist shows it separate on the table while right_wrist shows the pen still held. Frames 873–1399 in all three cameras show no completed assembly and prolonged inactivity. This is a visibly unsuccessful attempt, not merely unconfirmed completion at a recording cutoff.

failure_annotations.explanation: After bringing the held parts together, the robot continues an unsuccessful insertion: left_wrist at frames 434–536 shows the pen offset beside the cap rather than seated inside it. Gripper readjustments at frames 613–700 do not complete the assembly. During separation at frames 736–760, left_wrist shows the cap falling free and remaining on the table, while right_wrist shows the pen retained. The insertion and subsequent loss of cap retention disrupt the capping task; no hidden cause is established.
failure_annotations.recovery: Keep the pen secure, locate and regrasp the cap, align its opening with the pen tip in both wrist views, and insert gently before releasing either part; no human intervention appears necessary.
failure_annotations.severity_evidence: The small cap remains on the work surface; no breakage, damage or meaningful damage risk is visible in left_wrist and top at frames 748–766.
failure_annotations.resetability_evidence: Both required parts remain accessible, so another attempt can proceed by reacquiring the cap without a human environmental reset.

failure_annotations.explanation: After the repositioning ends, frames 873, 1000, 1200 and 1399 in left_wrist, right_wrist and top show essentially unchanged grippers and separate parts for over ten seconds. There is no renewed cap acquisition or insertion, establishing sustained unproductive stalling with the task incomplete.
failure_annotations.recovery: Resume by verifying the parts’ positions, acquiring the cap and establishing stable holds before attempting aligned insertion; human intervention is not visibly required.
failure_annotations.severity_evidence: The consequence is lack of task progress; the stationary scene shows no damage or additional physical disruption.
failure_annotations.resetability_evidence: Stalling introduces no environmental change requiring reset; task-directed actions can resume from the accessible parts’ current positions.
